question.worked_solution:
First, we put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals and then simplify the result:

$$
\sqrt{\frac{36}{121{t}^{2}}}=\frac{\sqrt{36}}{\sqrt{121{t}^{2}}}=\frac{\sqrt{{6}^{2}}}{\sqrt{121{t}^{2}}}=\frac{6}{\sqrt{121{t}^{2}}}
$$

Now, notice that the expression inside the radical is a perfect square. So, we can continue simplifying by writing the expression as this perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{\sqrt{121{t}^{2}}} & = \\ \frac{6}{\sqrt{(11t)^{2}}} & = \\ \frac{6}{|11t|} & = \\ \frac{6}{|11|\cdot |t|} & = \\ \frac{6}{11\cdot |t|}\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we are told that $t<0,$ so we have $|t|=-t.$ Therefore, the final answer is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{11\cdot |t|} & = \\ \frac{6}{11\cdot (-t)} & = \\ -\frac{6}{11t}.\end{aligned}
$$
